title: What can you say about iron in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 4 wordings for iron; the strongest is "Helps form red blood cells and haemoglobin" (strong, 1.4-45 mg elemental iron a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats anemia or iron deficiency anemia".

supported_wordings.wording: Helps form red blood cells and haemoglobin.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists red blood cell formation and the EU authorizes normal red blood cell and haemoglobin formation.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 1.4-45 mg elemental iron a day for adults 19 and older. EU: at least 2.1 mg, 15% of the 14 mg EU reference value (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII).
supported_wordings.form: Any iron form, counted as elemental iron

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats anemia or iron deficiency anemia

wordings_to_avoid.why: Promises a cure; the supported wording is less tiredness and fatigue.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition
